scenarios.title: A regeneration shield stays in place until a destruction uses it up

setup.notes: River Boa is not black, so Doom Blade can target it. Doom Blade does not say it can't be regenerated.

decisions: A casts the first Doom Blade targeting River Boa, tapping two Swamps.
A passes priority. B responds by activating River Boa's regeneration ability once ({G}, tapping one Forest). B does not activate it again.
Both players pass; the regeneration ability resolves and creates a shield. Both players pass again; the first Doom Blade resolves.
If River Boa is still on the battlefield, A casts the second Doom Blade targeting River Boa, tapping two Swamps. B takes no action; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: one_shield
variants.expected: The first Doom Blade's destruction is replaced: River Boa stays on the battlefield, tapped, and the shield is used up. The second Doom Blade resolves with no shield left and River Boa is destroyed and moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: two_shields
variants.delta: B activates the regeneration ability twice in response to the first Doom Blade, tapping both Forests.
variants.expected: Both shields stay in place until used: the first Doom Blade uses one and River Boa stays on the battlefield tapped; the second Doom Blade uses the other and River Boa is still on the battlefield. B's graveyard is empty.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: B activates the regeneration ability a second time.

variants.label: no_shield
variants.delta: B does not activate the regeneration ability.
variants.expected: The first Doom Blade resolves and River Boa is destroyed and moves to B's graveyard. No replacement applies.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: B does not activate the regeneration ability.

scenarios.forge_notes: Doom Blade's Forge script has no NoRegen parameter, unlike Terror, so regeneration works against it.

detector.outcome: A destruction event meets a regeneration-shield replacement and is replaced by regeneration.
detector.near_miss: A destruction event meets a replacement effect whose handler does not replace it, so the permanent is destroyed.

scenarios.title: A replacement effect must exist before the event; regeneration set up after the destruction changes nothing
decisions: A casts Doom Blade targeting River Boa, tapping two Swamps.
A passes priority. B responds by activating River Boa's regeneration ability ({G}, tapping the Forest); it resolves before Doom Blade. Then both players pass and Doom Blade resolves.

variants.label: in_response
variants.expected: The shield exists when Doom Blade's destruction would happen, so the destruction is replaced: River Boa stays on the battlefield, tapped. Doom Blade resolves and goes to A's graveyard.

variants.label: too_late
variants.delta: B passes without activating the regeneration ability.
variants.expected: Doom Blade resolves and River Boa is destroyed and moves to B's graveyard. River Boa is no longer on the battlefield, so its regeneration ability can no longer be activated and no shield exists.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: B does not activate the regeneration ability.

detector.outcome: A destruction event meets a replacement effect (regeneration shield) that already existed when it was proposed, and is replaced.
detector.near_miss: A destruction event meets a replacement effect whose handler does not replace it, so the permanent is destroyed.

scenarios.title: Each replacement effect applies at most once to an event, so two doublers make 2 damage into 8

setup.notes: Both copies of Furnace of Rath are on A's battlefield and are not tapped lands; they need no mana.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting B, tapping the Mountain.
Both players pass; Shock resolves.

variants.label: two_doublers
variants.expected: Shock's 2 damage is doubled once by each Furnace of Rath: B is dealt 8 damage, not 4 and not an unbounded amount. B's life total is 12.

variants.label: one_doubler
variants.delta: Only one Furnace of Rath is on A's battlefield.
variants.expected: Shock's 2 damage is doubled once: B is dealt 4 damage. B's life total is 16.

operation.unclassifiable: Removes a permanent: one Furnace of Rath leaves the battlefield.

variants.label: no_doubler
variants.delta: No Furnace of Rath is on A's battlefield.
variants.expected: B is dealt 2 damage. B's life total is 18.

operation.unclassifiable: Removes two permanents: both Furnaces of Rath leave the battlefield.

detector.outcome: A damage event's amount is modified by a replacement effect, each such effect applying at most once.
detector.near_miss: A damage event meets a replacement effect whose handler does not modify its amount.

scenarios.title: A replaced event never happens, so abilities that trigger on it do not trigger

Both players pass; Shock resolves.
If Blood Artist triggers, B targets A with it and both players pass.

variants.label: replaced
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is dealt 2 damage and would die, but Leyline of the Void exiles it instead. It never goes to the graveyard, so it does not die and Blood Artist does not trigger. Grizzly Bears is in exile; both life totals stay 20.

variants.label: no_replacement
variants.delta: Leyline of the Void is not on A's battlefield.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears dies and moves to B's graveyard. Blood Artist triggers: A loses 1 life and B gains 1 life. A's life is 19 and B's life is 21.

detector.outcome: A zone change to the graveyard is replaced by a replacement effect, so the original move never happens.
detector.near_miss: A zone change to the graveyard meets a replacement effect whose handler does not replace it, so the original move happens.

scenarios.title: The modified event is the one that happens and the abilities it triggers see its amount
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Boros Reckoner, tapping the Mountain.
Both players pass; Shock resolves.
Boros Reckoner's trigger goes on the stack; B targets A with it and both players pass.

variants.label: increased
variants.expected: Torbran replaces Shock's 2 damage with 4 damage, so Boros Reckoner (3/3) is dealt 4 damage and dies. Its trigger sees 4 damage and deals 4 damage to A. A's life is 16.

variants.label: not_replaced
variants.delta: Torbran, Thane of Red Fell is not on A's battlefield.
variants.expected: Boros Reckoner is dealt 2 damage and survives with 2 damage marked. Its trigger deals 2 damage to A. A's life is 18.

operation.unclassifiable: Removes a permanent: Torbran is not on the battlefield.

detector.outcome: A damage event is modified by a replacement effect and the modified event is the one that happens.
detector.near_miss: A damage event meets a replacement effect whose handler does not modify it, so it is dealt as proposed.

scenarios.title: A regeneration shield does nothing when the destruction it would replace never happens
decisions: A casts Doom Blade targeting River Boa, tapping two Swamps, and passes priority.
B responds by activating River Boa's regeneration ability ({G}, tapping the Forest).
B then casts Boros Charm choosing the mode 'permanents you control gain indestructible until end of turn', tapping the Mountain and the Plains.
All players pass until the stack is empty: Boros Charm resolves, then the regeneration ability, then Doom Blade.

variants.label: indestructible
variants.expected: River Boa is indestructible when Doom Blade resolves, so the destruction never happens and the regeneration shield has nothing to replace. River Boa stays on the battlefield untapped; the shield is not used.

variants.label: regenerates
variants.delta: B does not cast Boros Charm.
variants.expected: Doom Blade's destruction is replaced by the regeneration shield: River Boa stays on the battlefield and is tapped by the shield.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: B does not cast Boros Charm.

scenarios.forge_notes: Assumes Forge checks indestructible before the regeneration replacement is applied, which is what the untapped/tapped contrast tests.

detector.none: The rule's outcome is a replacement effect left unused because its event never happened. An unused replacement writes no rewrite record (one is written per executeReplacement call, and an event that never happens calls none), and a Destroy resolution's effect half lacks a destroyed event both when indestructible stops the destruction and when a regeneration shield replaces it, so no field separates the two sides.

scenarios.title: A source dealing 0 damage deals no damage, so a damage-increasing effect has nothing to replace
decisions: A casts Blaze with X = 0 targeting B, tapping one Mountain.
Both players pass; Blaze resolves.

variants.label: x_zero
variants.expected: Blaze deals no damage, so there is no damage event for Torbran to increase. B's life total stays 20.

variants.label: x_one
variants.delta: A casts Blaze with X = 1, tapping both Mountains.
variants.expected: Blaze deals 1 damage, which Torbran increases by 2 to 3. B's life total is 17.

operation.unclassifiable: A different choice by a player: X = 1 instead of 0, paid with a second Mountain.

detector.none: The scenario is rewrite-kind, and a 0-damage source writes no rewrite record: Forge's damage replacement list skips a damage amount of 0, so no damage replacement is ever checked against it. The absence shows only in a resolution record (a DealDamage effect half with no damage_dealt event), which rewrite-kind detectors never read.

scenarios.title: Regeneration removes damage, taps the creature and removes it from combat

setup.notes: White Knight has first strike and protection from black. River Boa is green.

decisions: A attacks B with White Knight.
B blocks White Knight with River Boa.
In the declare blockers step, after blocks, B activates River Boa's regeneration ability ({G}, tapping the Forest). Both players pass until it resolves.
Both players pass; combat damage is dealt (first-strike step, then regular step).

variants.label: regenerates
variants.expected: White Knight deals 2 first-strike damage to River Boa (toughness 1), which would be destroyed; regeneration replaces that: River Boa stays on the battlefield with no damage marked, tapped, and removed from combat. It deals no combat damage to White Knight, which has no damage. B's life stays 20.

variants.label: no_regeneration
variants.delta: B does not activate the regeneration ability.
variants.expected: White Knight deals 2 first-strike damage to River Boa, which is destroyed and moves to B's graveyard. White Knight has no damage. B's life stays 20.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: B does not activate the regeneration ability.

detector.outcome: A destruction event is replaced by regeneration, which removes damage, taps the permanent and removes it from combat.
detector.near_miss: A destruction event meets a replacement effect whose handler does not replace it, so the permanent is destroyed and nothing removes its damage or takes it out of combat.

scenarios.title: Damage triggers still trigger when the damaged permanent regenerates

setup.notes: Kazarov, Sengir Pureblood has no counters at the start.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting River Boa, tapping the Mountain, and passes priority.
B responds by activating River Boa's regeneration ability ({G}, tapping the Forest); it resolves.
Both players pass; A's spell resolves.

variants.label: damage_regenerated
variants.expected: Shock deals 2 damage to River Boa, so Kazarov triggers and gets a +1/+1 counter (5/5). River Boa would be destroyed and regenerates: it stays on the battlefield, tapped, with no damage marked.

variants.label: destroy_no_damage
variants.delta: A casts Doom Blade (tapping both Swamps) instead of Shock.
variants.expected: Doom Blade deals no damage, so Kazarov does not trigger and stays 4/4. River Boa's destruction is replaced by regeneration: it stays on the battlefield, tapped.

operation.unclassifiable: A different spell cast: Doom Blade instead of Shock.

detector.outcome: A trigger on damage done is evaluated and fires for damage dealt to a permanent, whether or not the permanent is then destroyed or regenerates.
detector.near_miss: A damage-done trigger is evaluated against an event it does not match and does not fire.

Both players pass; Shock resolves.

variants.label: redirected
variants.expected: Palisade Giant redirects the damage: Palisade Giant (2/7) is dealt 2 damage and survives with 2 marked. Grizzly Bears has no damage and stays on the battlefield.

variants.label: not_covered
variants.delta: Shock targets A's own Hill Giant instead of Grizzly Bears.

scenarios.title: A redirection whose recipient has left the battlefield does nothing

setup.notes: Daughter of Autumn is green, so Doom Blade can target it. Glory Seeker is a white 2/2.

decisions: A casts Shock targeting Glory Seeker, tapping the Mountain, and passes priority.
B responds by activating Daughter of Autumn's ability ({W}, tapping the Plains) targeting Glory Seeker; both players pass and it resolves.
A receives priority and passes.
Both players pass; Shock resolves.

variants.label: redirected
variants.expected: Of Shock's 2 damage, 1 is dealt to Daughter of Autumn instead of Glory Seeker: Daughter of Autumn has 1 damage marked, Glory Seeker has 1 damage marked, and both stay on the battlefield.

variants.label: recipient_gone
variants.delta: When A receives priority after Daughter's ability resolves, A casts Doom Blade targeting Daughter of Autumn (tapping both Swamps) and it resolves before Shock.
variants.expected: Daughter of Autumn is in B's graveyard when Shock resolves, so the redirection does nothing: Glory Seeker is dealt 2 damage and moves to B's graveyard.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: A casts an extra spell, Doom Blade, before Shock resolves.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge scripts Daughter of Autumn's shield as an effect with Duration UntilHostLeavesPlayOrEOT and ExileOnMoved, so the shield is removed when Daughter leaves; the observable damage matches the rule.

scenarios.title: A skip effect makes the next combat phase not happen, but not one that has already started
decisions: In the main phase, before combat, A casts Moment of Silence targeting A, tapping the Plains; both players pass and it resolves.
A attacks B with Grizzly Bears in any combat phase that occurs.

variants.label: skip_own_combat
variants.expected: A's combat phase is skipped: there is no beginning of combat, no attack and no combat damage. B's life stays 20.

variants.label: combat_already_started
variants.delta: A attacks with Grizzly Bears first, then casts Moment of Silence targeting A during the declare attackers step.
variants.expected: The combat phase has already started, so it is not skipped; no later combat phase this turn exists to skip. Grizzly Bears deals 2 combat damage and B's life is 18.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: A casts Moment of Silence during the declare attackers step instead of the main phase.

variants.label: skip_other_player
variants.delta: In the main phase, A casts Moment of Silence targeting B.
variants.expected: The skip applies to B's next combat phase this turn, which does not exist on A's turn. A's combat phase happens: Grizzly Bears deals 2 combat damage and B's life is 18.

operation.unclassifiable: A different target: Moment of Silence targets B instead of A.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge implements Moment of Silence as a SkipPhase effect with Duration NextThisTurn.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: A plays the Breeding Pool from hand instead of from the library.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's Breeding Pool pays life through an UnlessCost, which may not go through the PayLife replacement; Ashiok's exile effect uses NotDefinedReplacedSimultaneousETB to leave out the entering card.

detector.none: The outcome is that a card entering from the library is left out of an exile-from-the-top replacement, an exclusion; no record field shows which objects a replacement did not apply to.

scenarios.title: A linked ability refers only to cards exiled by the replacement event of the ability it is linked to
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping the Mountain; both players pass until it resolves.
A then tries to activate Void Maw's ability, putting a card exiled with Void Maw into its owner's graveyard as the cost.

variants.label: exiled_by_replacement
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears would die; Void Maw exiles it instead. The activation is legal: A puts Grizzly Bears into B's graveyard as the cost and Void Maw gets +2/+2 until end of turn (6/7).

variants.label: exiled_by_spell
variants.delta: A casts Swords to Plowshares targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping the Plains.
variants.expected: Swords to Plowshares exiles Grizzly Bears; it was not exiled by Void Maw's replacement, so it is not exiled with Void Maw. B gains 2 life. The activation is not legal: A has no card exiled with Void Maw to pay the cost.

operation.unclassifiable: A different spell cast: Swords to Plowshares instead of Shock.

detector.none: The link between a card exiled by a replacement event and the ability that refers to it is in no record field; a playability candidate lists its verdict bits and targets but not the objects a linked ability refers to.

scenarios.title: A self-replacement effect applies before other replacement effects to the same event
decisions: A casts Fiery Impulse targeting Ironroot Treefolk, tapping the Mountain.
Both players pass; Fiery Impulse resolves.

variants.label: mastery_then_doubled
variants.expected: Spell mastery is on (two instants in A's graveyard): the self-replacement makes the damage 3 first, then Furnace of Rath doubles it to 6. Ironroot Treefolk (3/5) is dealt 6 damage and moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: no_mastery
variants.delta: A's graveyard holds only Shock.
variants.expected: Only one instant is in the graveyard, so the damage is 2, doubled by Furnace of Rath to 4. Ironroot Treefolk survives with 4 damage marked.

operation.unclassifiable: Changes a graveyard: Lightning Bolt is not in A's graveyard.

variants.label: no_doubler
variants.delta: Furnace of Rath is not on A's battlefield.
variants.expected: Spell mastery makes the damage 3. Ironroot Treefolk survives with 3 damage marked.

operation.unclassifiable: Removes a permanent: Furnace of Rath is not on the battlefield.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge scripts Fiery Impulse's spell mastery as a conditional second DealDamage, not as a replacement effect; the observable damage is the same.

detector.none: Forge has no self-replacement layer (ReplacementLayer is CantHappen, Control, Copy, Transform, Other) and scripts a self-replacement inside the spell's own ability as a conditional parameter, so no rewrite record is written for it; the other replacement's rewrite and the resolution's damage_dealt amount do not say which of the two applied first.

scenarios.title: A token-creation replacement also applies to tokens created by another replacement effect
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping the Mountain.
Both players pass; Shock resolves.

variants.label: doubled
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears would die; Kalitas exiles it instead and creates a 2/2 Zombie token. Parallel Lives applies to that token creation, so A creates two 2/2 Zombie tokens.

variants.label: single
variants.delta: Parallel Lives is not on A's battlefield.
variants.expected: Kalitas exiles Grizzly Bears and A creates one 2/2 Zombie token.

operation.unclassifiable: Removes a permanent: Parallel Lives is not on the battlefield.

detector.outcome: A token-creation event, including one produced by another replacement effect, is modified by a token-creation replacement effect.
detector.near_miss: A token-creation event meets a token replacement whose handler does not modify it.

scenarios.title: A can't effect stops only what happens after it exists
decisions: A casts Skullcrack targeting B, tapping both Mountains.
Both players pass; Skullcrack resolves.
A passes priority; B casts Healing Salve choosing 'target player gains 3 life' targeting B, tapping the Plains.
Both players pass; Healing Salve resolves.

variants.label: after
variants.expected: Skullcrack's effect already exists, so B can't gain life: Healing Salve resolves and B gains no life. B took 3 damage from Skullcrack: B's life total is 7.

variants.label: in_response
variants.delta: B casts Healing Salve in response to Skullcrack, while Skullcrack is still on the stack.
variants.expected: The can't effect does not exist yet, so Healing Salve resolves first and B gains 3 life (13). Skullcrack then deals 3 damage: B's life total is 10.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: B casts Healing Salve in response to Skullcrack instead of after it.

detector.none: The scenario is rewrite-kind, and a can't-gain-life effect is a static (Mode$ CantGainLife), not a replacement, so no rewrite record is written on either side. The withheld gain shows only in a resolution record (a GainLife effect half with no life_change event), which rewrite-kind detectors never read.

scenarios.title: A player cannot choose to pay a cost that includes an event that can't happen

setup.notes: A controls no lands. Mutagenic Growth costs {G/P}, which can be paid with 2 life instead of {G}.

decisions: A considers casting Mutagenic Growth targeting Grizzly Bears, paying {G/P} with 2 life.

variants.label: emperion_controlled
variants.expected: Platinum Emperion means A's life total can't change, so A can't pay 2 life. A has no mana, so Mutagenic Growth is not castable.

variants.label: emperion_opponent
variants.delta: Platinum Emperion is on B's battlefield instead.
variants.expected: A's life total can change, so A can pay 2 life for {G/P}. Mutagenic Growth is castable.

operation.unclassifiable: Changes a permanent's controller: Platinum Emperion is B's instead of A's, which no fork operation makes.

scenarios.title: An event that can't happen is not modified by a replacement effect
decisions: A casts Skullcrack targeting B, tapping two Mountains; both players pass and it resolves.
A casts Healing Salve choosing 'target player gains 3 life' targeting A, tapping the Plains.
Both players pass; Healing Salve resolves.

variants.label: cant_gain
variants.expected: Skullcrack makes it so players can't gain life this turn, so the life gain can't happen and Rain of Gore's replacement does not turn it into life loss. A's life stays 20; B's life is 17 from Skullcrack.

variants.label: replaced
variants.delta: A does not cast Skullcrack.
variants.expected: The life gain can happen, so Rain of Gore replaces it: A loses 3 life instead. A's life is 17 and B's life is 20.

operation.unclassifiable: A different player decision: A does not cast Skullcrack.

scenarios.forge_notes: Assumes Forge checks the CantGainLife static ability before applying the GainLife replacement.

detector.none: The scenario is rewrite-kind, and on its fires side the life gain can't happen, so no GainLife replacement is checked and no rewrite record is written; a rewrite with result replaced exists only on the near-miss side. The outcome shows only in a resolution record (a GainLife effect half with no life_change event), which rewrite-kind detectors never read.

scenarios.title: A can't effect on entering can stop a permanent from entering the battlefield
decisions: A casts Zombify targeting Grizzly Bears in A's graveyard, tapping four Swamps.
Both players pass; Zombify resolves.

variants.label: cage
variants.expected: Grafdigger's Cage means creature cards in graveyards can't enter the battlefield: Grizzly Bears stays in A's graveyard. Zombify goes to A's graveyard.

variants.label: no_cage
variants.delta: Grafdigger's Cage is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears enters the battlefield under A's control. Zombify goes to A's graveyard.

operation.unclassifiable: Removes a permanent: Grafdigger's Cage is not on the battlefield.

detector.outcome: A zone change to the battlefield from a graveyard or library is prevented by a replacement effect that says it can't happen.
detector.near_miss: A move to the battlefield meets a replacement effect whose handler does not prevent it, so the permanent enters.
